item.title: [Due in 4 days] Exchange Online Admin API v2.0 drops Exchange.ManageV2 and Exchange.ManageAsAppV2 on 1 December; apps must move to Exchange.AdminAPI.Manage / .ManageAsApp and get fresh admin consent
item.description:
Every automation and third-party tool that administers Exchange through the Admin API needs a new consent grant this month; a rushed tenant-wide consent on an app-only Exchange administration permission is exactly the grant an attacker hopes to slip through, and a missed one breaks the tool on 1 December.

Exchange Online · deadline 2026-12-01 · Inventory service principals holding Exchange.ManageV2 or Exchange.ManageAsAppV2, grant the replacement only to apps you still need, verify their Exchange RBAC role, test, then remove the old permission before 1 December; alert on consent to Exchange.AdminAPI.ManageAsApp in AuditLogs.

item.title: [Due in 3 days] Outlook's Join button stops appearing for meetings whose join URL is HTTP-only, from the week of 30 November 2026
item.description:
An HTTP-only meeting link is a cleartext redirect target; dropping the button removes one click path to it, and an integration still emitting HTTP links is worth finding.

Exchange Online · deadline 2026-11-30 · Ask owners of third-party meeting providers, add-ins and custom integrations to confirm they emit HTTPS join URLs, and validate new invitations before 30 November 2026.

item.title: [New] Outlook for iOS, Android and Mac move Contact Support under the new Outlook cloud policy; tenants that disabled it must redeploy the policy
item.description:
A support chat inside the mail client is a channel users trust; tenants that switched it off for data-handling reasons will see it come back on mobile and Mac unless the policy is redeployed.

Exchange Online · If you disabled Contact Support in new Outlook, redeploy that Cloud Policy once the updated version appears in OCPS so it also covers iOS, Android and Mac.

item.title: [Message Center] MC1562272 New Contact Support Experience in Outlook for iOS, Android and Mac
item.description:
A new Contact Support experience is rolling out in Outlook for iOS, Android, and Mac, aligning with the new Outlook for Windows. It uses the existing policy "Allow access to Contact Support in the new Outlook." Rollout starts late November 2026, completing by January 2027. No new policy needed; admins with disabled policies must redeploy.
